description: Complete the Electron-to-native Rust+GPUI rewrite with UI/UX parity, runtime contract completion, and native verification.

userStories.title: Rebuild native shell, onboarding, dashboard, sidebar, and messages surfaces
userStories.description: As an operator, I want the core shell surfaces to match the original product grammar so that the native app feels familiar and production-ready.
acceptanceCriteria: Native shell, sidebar, onboarding, dashboard, and messages surfaces are implemented in GPUI
UI hierarchy follows the original Electron product surfaces
userStories.notes: Completed in commits 301934a and earlier parity work.

userStories.title: Rebuild approvals and documents native surfaces
userStories.description: As an operator, I want approvals and documents to match the original information architecture so that review and document workflows stay intuitive.
acceptanceCriteria: Approvals surface matches the original sectioned layout
Documents surface matches the original document center grammar

userStories.title: Rebuild runs and inbox native surfaces
userStories.description: As an operator, I want run inspection and attention queues to match the original app so that active work remains legible at a glance.
acceptanceCriteria: Runs queue and detail layout are implemented in GPUI
Inbox attention groups are implemented in GPUI

userStories.title: Rebuild settings and workspaces native surfaces
userStories.description: As an operator, I want settings and workspace management to match the original desktop structure so that control-plane tasks remain consistent.
acceptanceCriteria: Settings shell is represented as a sectioned native surface
Workspaces are represented as a native list surface

userStories.title: Extend native persistence verification for aligned surfaces
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want native storage-backed verification so that rebuilt surfaces rest on stable persisted state.
acceptanceCriteria: Storage-backed end-to-end test covers reviews, approvals, runs, and documents

userStories.title: Implement native settings mutations and workspace interactions
userStories.description: As an operator, I want settings and workspace surfaces to perform real actions so that the native app controls production state end-to-end.
acceptanceCriteria: Settings theme/locale/execution mode/provider/data actions are wired to real Rust-side state transitions or bridge actions
Workspace selection and primary workspace interactions are backed by real state changes
userStories.notes: Completed with real settings/workspace mutations and snapshot-backed verification.

userStories.title: Add native animation and interaction-state parity
userStories.description: As an operator, I want the native app to preserve the original motion, hover, selection, and attention behavior so that the product feels identical in use.
acceptanceCriteria: Core surfaces implement matching hover, selection, and emphasis states
Onboarding, inbox, messages, and dashboard include native motion/state treatment aligned with Electron references

userStories.title: Complete runtime contract integration into native app flows
userStories.description: As an operator, I want Pi Mono run, steer, follow-up, approval, and artifact events to drive the native UI so that the app is a complete replacement for Electron.
acceptanceCriteria: Run lifecycle events are surfaced in native UI from real runtime data
Approval gates participate in real runtime flows
Message and artifact updates reflect live runtime contract events
userStories.notes: Core completion story for full replacement.

userStories.title: Add final native end-to-end verification matrix
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want a broader native verification matrix so that the rewritten app can be trusted as the production desktop path.
acceptanceCriteria: Native tests cover onboarding bootstrap, run inspection, approval visibility, document visibility, settings/workspace state, and inbox attention derivation
userStories.notes: Final confidence layer before calling the rewrite complete.
